_note: Default settings for the decision engine (DESIGN.md O). Every number is a typical value or a placeholder for the farm's own; 'source' says which. Edit freely.

awc_in_per_ft.source: typical silt loam plant-available water (USDA NRCS soil surveys); sand ~1.0, loam ~1.8

root_ft.source: managed root zone for corn, typical extension guidance

p.source: FAO-56 (Allen et al. 1998) depletion fraction for maize

et_peak.source: peak corn water use in hot, dry weather, ~0.30-0.35 in/day (Great Plains extension guidance)

gpm_per_acre.source: pivot capacity; typical Nebraska 4-7 gpm/acre. Use your own

ky.source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos & Kassam 1979) yield response factor, maize around flowering (1.25 whole season)

season_et.source: seasonal corn water use, inches, typical

price.source: PLACEHOLDER: your expected price, $/bu (or a December futures quote)

pump_cost_per_in.source: PLACEHOLDER: your pumping cost per acre-inch (energy and wear; varies widely)

spell_days.source: length of the dry spell simulated

reaction_days.source: PLACEHOLDER: days after stress begins that you'd normally start (sensor or crop symptoms)

false_alarm_waste.source: PLACEHOLDER: share of water pumped ahead of a dry spell that never comes that is wasted (rain refills the profile)

review_days.source: days you'd keep the pivot on before re-deciding if no dry spell comes

hay.label: Buy hay or feed before prices rise
hay.note: Partly zero-sum between neighbours (James): buying early moves the price rise onto someone else. The market tends to move when the Drought Monitor shows drought, a median 22 days after the soil crosses the drought line (eval/lead.py), so most of the value comes from acting before the market, and extra days of notice matter less.

tons.source: PLACEHOLDER: hay you'd need to buy

drought_rise.source: PLACEHOLDER: price rise in a drought year, share

carry_cost_share.source: PLACEHOLDER: storage loss and interest if bought and not needed this season

nitrogen.label: Trim side-dress nitrogen
nitrogen.note: Extension advice (NC State 2026, Wisconsin, Ohio State) is to keep the planned rate unless drought has cut yield potential; a flash-drought warning is the early sign that it may. So a trim, not a skip, and only on rain-fed corn.

n_cut_lb.source: Trim of a typical 40-60 lb side-dress; large cuts are not advised

n_price_per_lb.source: USDA AMS Iowa production cost report, June 2026: anhydrous ammonia $1,085 a ton

yield_cost_if_wrong_pct.source: Estimate: yield lost from a 30 lb trim if rain comes and the crop needed it

yield_bu.source: Rain-fed corn, typical; the farm page uses USDA county yields

fungicide_corn.label: Skip the fungicide pass (corn)
fungicide_corn.note: Foliar fungicide at tasseling/silking. Iowa State: average gain 3.3 bu/acre over 26 sites, profitable 27% of the time; responses are larger with disease and wet weather and near zero in dry seasons (NC State 2024 drought trial: no significant gain). Ohio State: ~$40/acre product and application; Wisconsin ~$22.

cost_per_acre.source: Product and application, between Wisconsin ($22) and Ohio State ($40)

response_wet_bu.source: Gain when disease is present and it stays wet (fields you'd normally spray)

response_dry_bu.source: Gain in a dry spell: little disease (NC State 2024 drought trial)

fungicide_soy.label: Skip the fungicide pass (soybeans)
fungicide_soy.note: Foliar fungicide at R3. Responses smaller than corn, again largest with disease and wet weather.

response_wet_bu.source: Gain when disease is present and it stays wet, estimate

response_dry_bu.source: Gain in a dry spell, estimate

silage.label: Get ready to chop drought-hit corn for silage
silage.note: For livestock farms. Drought-hit corn is still feed if chopped at the right moisture (60-70%); it often looks drier than it is, so test before chopping (Minnesota and Wisconsin extension). Notice gives time to line up a chopper, storage and moisture tests. Rough estimates.

silage_t_per_acre.source: Drought-hit corn silage yield, tons an acre (estimate)

kept_share.source: Feed value kept by chopping on time rather than late (estimate)

prep_cost_per_acre.source: Booking and testing if no drought comes (estimate)
